senses.gloss: f. (חָנַךְ) [rubbing the infant’s palate with a chewed fig, v. Fl. to Levy Talm. Dict. II, 206,] the name given to the child by the person rubbing is palate; in gen. surname.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 9:8">Gitt. IX, 8</cite> <he>כתב חֲנִיכָתוֹ וחֲנִיכָתָהּ</he> if in the letter of divorce his and her family names are written.
<cite ref="Gittin 88a">Ib. 88ᵃ</cite> <he>הֲנִיכַת אבות</he> the surname of ancestors.

Taan. 20ᵇ; Meg. 28ᵃ I never called my neighbor בחֲנִיכָתִי וא״ל בחֲנִיכָתוֹ (Ar.) by an opprobrious surname given him by myself or, as others relate, by his by-name (which others had given him); ed.: בהכינתו וא״ל בחניכתו by his ḥăkhina (v. הֲכִינָה); some say, (Rab Ada used the expression) ḥăkhina.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 25b:9">M. Kat. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>בעת חֲנִיכָתוֹ אבד חַנִּיכוֹ</he> (Ms. M. 2) at the time when he was to receive his name (when his palate was rubbed) died he who was to rear him (his father); (ed., v. <cite ref="H01293"><he>חֲנִינָה</he> II</cite>).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 43">Gen. R. s. 43</cite>, beg. (expl. <he>חניכיו</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 14:14">Gen. XIV, 14</cite>) <he>בעלי חֲנִיכָתוֹ וכ׳</he> those bearing his name, their name being Abram, like his own.
